subagent_reports.topic: Discovery opportunity scout: remote owner routing for ADV Epic/change target_path tools (issue #195)

sources.label: adv_change_create target_path short-circuit
sources.summary: When target_path is set, create routes into createCrossProjectFollowUp BEFORE the Epic seed logic at lines 1205-1231, so epic_id/entry_id/epic_title are silently dropped.

sources.label: createCrossProjectFollowUp metadata
sources.summary: targetStore.changes.create is the authoritative write and IS correctly target-routed, but initialMetadata only carries cross_project_origin; epic_membership is never forwarded. Fix is narrow metadata forwarding.

sources.label: adv_epic_create lacks target routing
sources.summary: adv_epic_create has no target_path/target_confirmed/confirmationEvidence args, so creating an Epic in Project A from Project B is impossible. Same gap for show/list/update.

sources.label: Owner-local Epic vs target child projection
sources.summary: link/move/unlink/repair route only the child projection to childStore.store; Epic lookup (loadEpic(store)) and mutation (store.epics.linkChange) stay owner-local by deliberate design (test 'routes child projection through target_path while Epic remains owner-local'). Issue #195 EPIC_NOT_FOUND arises because the Epic lives in the target, not the local session store.

sources.label: Reusable target routing primitive
sources.summary: targetPathSchema, withTargetPathStore, and appendTargetProjectContextOutput already exist and are used by Epic link/move/repair; remote-owner routing can reuse them.

sources.label: advance-epics spec project-aware entries
sources.summary: Change entries support a project-aware change_ref carrying change_id, project_id, optional repo_id, and optional target_path; one-Epic-per-change and optional membership invariants remain authoritative.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: The existing cross-project Epic model is a deliberate 'owner-local Epic + target child projection' split shape, encoded in epic.test.ts:625: link/move/unlink/repair route only the child change projection to the target store while the Epic itself is looked up and mutated in the current-session-local store. Issue #195 asks for a different shape — 'remote owner routing' where the Epic ALSO lives in the target project. Two concrete defects follow: (1) adv_change_create target_path silently drops Epic seed fields because it short-circuits into createCrossProjectFollowUp, which never forwards epic_membership into the (correctly target-routed) targetStore.changes.create; this is a narrow, low-risk fix. (2) adv_epic_create/show/list/update have no target_path args at all, and link/move/unlink/repair look up the Epic in the wrong (local) store for the remote-owner case, producing misleading EPIC_NOT_FOUND. The reusable withTargetPathStore/targetPathSchema primitive already exists, so the create-side fix and epic_create routing are cheap. The unresolved architectural fork is whether a single target_path can mean 'authoritative for both Epic owner and child' (colliding with the existing owner-local split-project design) or whether distinct owner/child target fields plus a supported/unsupported routing matrix are required — this needs a user/orchestrator decision before implementation.

validation.notes: No hard blocker, but a supported-shape decision is a prerequisite. The existing owner-local split-project design (test-encoded at epic.test.ts:625) and issue #195's remote-owner shape both key off one target_path field and cannot be disambiguated without an explicit routing matrix decision. Recommend surfacing candidate 3 to the user before implementing candidates 2-4. Candidates 1 and 5 (seed forwarding + regression fixtures) are safe to adopt now regardless of the matrix decision.

tradeoffs: Single target_path is simple but conflates two distinct shapes (owner-local child-target split vs remote-owner); distinct owner/child target fields are more explicit but add schema surface and operator complexity.

Routing the Epic owner store to target for link/move/repair fixes EPIC_NOT_FOUND for the remote-owner case but conflicts with the deliberate owner-local design in epic.test.ts:625, forcing either a shape flag or a routing matrix.

Forwarding Epic seed metadata in createCrossProjectFollowUp is low-risk and reuses the existing local seed shape, but leaves the read/list Epic tools (show/list/update) still local-only unless separately routed.

alternatives_considered.option: Single target_path means authoritative for both Epic owner and child (remote-owner default)
alternatives_considered.rationale: Cleanest for the issue #195 use case but silently changes the existing owner-local split-project behavior encoded in epic.test.ts:625; requires user decision.

alternatives_considered.option: Distinct owner/child target fields + typed supported/unsupported routing matrix with pre-mutation rejection
alternatives_considered.rationale: Structurally correct (P33): makes both shapes explicit, fails unsupported splits before durable mutation with an actionable error instead of misleading EPIC_NOT_FOUND or orphaned changes.

alternatives_considered.option: Only fix the create-side seed drop and leave Epic mutation tools owner-local
alternatives_considered.rationale: Does not satisfy the User Outcome that an operator in Project B can create/link/repair an Epic that lives in Project A; leaves EPIC_NOT_FOUND unresolved.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Adopt candidates 1 (forward Epic seed into createCrossProjectFollowUp metadata) and 5 (issue #195 regression fixtures) now — both low-risk and shape-agnostic. Surface candidate 3 (route Epic owner store to target) to the user to decide the routing matrix: single target_path meaning both vs distinct owner/child fields. Gate candidates 2 (add target routing to adv_epic_create/show/list/update) and 4 (typed supported/unsupported routing matrix with pre-mutation rejection) on that decision. Reuse the existing withTargetPathStore/targetPathSchema primitive throughout.

subagent_reports.recommendation: Discovery should record 5 candidates: auto-adopt seed-forwarding (candidate 1) and regression fixtures (candidate 5); design-around adv_epic_create target routing (candidate 2) and the routing-matrix typed guard (candidate 4); and surface-to-user the owner-store routing fork (candidate 3) because it conflicts with the deliberate owner-local design in epic.test.ts:625 and matches the open Discovery Agenda question 'whether one target_path can safely mean authoritative target for all same-target operations, or whether distinct owner/child target fields are needed'.

sources.label: Reusable child-store resolver pattern

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: The draft design is structurally sound and reuses the right primitives (withTargetPathStore, resolveChildStore shape, maybeAppendTargetContext). Scouting surfaced five leverage points. (1) The single highest-payoff/lowest-risk shortcut: the create-side seed-drop fix is genuinely one-line forwarding — the storage layer (store-disk.ts:398-399, changes.ts:152/224) already accepts initialMetadata.epic_membership, so createCrossProjectFollowUp only needs to receive and forward the assembled membership; no new plumbing. (2) The design's resolveEpicOwnerStore should be built as a near-verbatim clone of resolveChildStore (epic.ts:339-361) rather than a fresh helper, keeping locality (P04) and matching the existing {context,store} contract that maybeAppendTargetContext already consumes. (3) The wrong-store defect is systemic, not per-tool: 8+ loadEpic(store,...) sites share one root cause; routing them through a single ownerStore accessor is a cross-cutting improvement that fixes AC4/DONT4 in one structural move and prevents whack-a-mole. (4) The seed-drop fix has an ordering subtlety worth calling out in design: the Epic-seed assembly currently lives AFTER the target_path branch (change.ts:1205-1231), so the fix must hoist seed validation/assembly ABOVE line 1158 or duplicate it inside the cross-project branch — otherwise AC1's 'validate parent Epic before target child creation / no orphan' cannot be satisfied because the branch returns before seed logic runs. (5) Parent-Epic pre-validation for the cross-project create should reuse the owner-store loadEpic path plus the existing INVALID_EPIC_MEMBERSHIP_SEED completeness guard (change.ts:1215) so SC3 is enforced structurally with no new error taxonomy. None of these alter the approved contract; all tie to existing AC/constraints.

validation.notes: No blockers. Design is adoptable. Two design-around notes: (a) hoist Epic-seed validation/assembly above the target_path branch so AC1/SC3 orphan-prevention is reachable on the cross-project path; (b) route all 8+ loadEpic sites through the single owner-store accessor to close AC4/DONT4 systemically. Both are within approved scope and low risk. Candidate 5 (parent-Epic pre-validation) is contract-tied to SC3 and must land with the create-side fix; treat as one unit.

tradeoffs: Cloning resolveChildStore into resolveEpicOwnerStore duplicates ~20 lines but preserves the proven {context,store} contract and avoids a premature shared abstraction; a later refactor could unify both behind one resolveScopedStore(kind) if a third store family appears.

Routing all loadEpic sites through an owner accessor touches 8+ call sites in one change (wider diff) but is the only way to make AC4/DONT4 structural rather than per-tool heuristic (P33); leaving any site owner-local reintroduces the misleading EPIC_NOT_FOUND.

Hoisting Epic-seed assembly above the target_path branch slightly reorders change.ts create flow, but the seed-completeness guard is pure validation with no side effects, so hoisting is safe and makes SC3 reachable on the cross-project path.

alternatives_considered.option: Build a fresh generic resolveScopedStore abstraction now instead of cloning resolveChildStore
alternatives_considered.rationale: Only two store families (owner, child) exist; a generic abstraction is speculative (YAGNI/P29). Clone the proven pattern; unify later only if a third family emerges.

alternatives_considered.option: Fix loadEpic wrong-store per-tool as each Epic operation is touched
alternatives_considered.rationale: Per-tool patching leaves other loadEpic(store,...) sites owner-local and reintroduces misleading EPIC_NOT_FOUND; the single owner-accessor route is structurally correct and closes AC4/DONT4 once.

alternatives_considered.option: Duplicate Epic-seed assembly inside the cross-project branch instead of hoisting it
alternatives_considered.rationale: Works but duplicates the completeness guard and INVALID_EPIC_MEMBERSHIP_SEED logic; hoisting above line 1158 is cleaner and keeps one seed-validation path. Design author's call, both satisfy AC1.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Adopt candidates 1 (seed-forwarding shortcut, trivial given storage already accepts it), 2 (clone resolveChildStore for resolveEpicOwnerStore), 3 (single owner-store accessor for all loadEpic sites), and 5 (reuse loadEpic+existing seed guard for parent-Epic pre-validation) into the design now — all contract-tied and low risk. Surface candidate 4 (unify both resolvers behind one generic helper) as follow-up only, not this change.

The proposed fix — a second explicit owner routing field family (epic_owner_target_path/target_confirmed/confirmationEvidence) resolved through a resolveEpicOwnerStore clone of the proven resolveChildStore→withTargetPathStore pattern — is structurally sound, reuses existing trust+queue-readiness+cache invariants, and keeps target_path child semantics backward-compatible (anchored by epic.test.ts:625). KD4's hoist of seed validation and epic_membership forwarding before the cross-project create branch is necessary and correctly targeted for AC1/SC3/DONT1. Typed pre-mutation error codes, distinct output contexts, and DDC store-identity assertions make correctness structural per C2/P33. No spec-law contradiction found; the design explicitly complies with rq-epicMembershipRepair01 cross-project trust rules and preserves optional membership + one-Epic-per-change invariants.

validation.notes: All KD claims source-verified. KD2 owner accessor, KD3 child-store independence, and KD4 hoist each map to confirmed code sites. Non-blocking cautions: (1) KD3 'omitted child route only when implementation can structurally prove same-owner child' is under-specified — planning must define the deterministic same-owner proof rather than inferring from target_path (DONT2 risk if implemented loosely). (2) Two-remote-store non-atomicity is acknowledged; preflight-before-mutation mitigates but link/move that mutate owner Epic then child projection can still leave projection_pending on child-store failure — ensure deterministic repair status is emitted on that exact partial path (rq-epicMembershipRepair01 compliance). (3) adv_epic_promote_shell remote-child case is scoped out via UNSUPPORTED_EPIC_ROUTING_SHAPE, which is acceptable but must be covered by a typed-error test so it fails before mutation, not mid-operation.

tradeoffs: Public tool schema grows by three owner-routing fields on many Epic tools plus adv_change_create — more surface to document and schema-test, mitigated by generated schema drift checks.
Two independent target stores are not transactionally atomic; correctness depends on preflight-before-mutation and deterministic repair statuses rather than a single transaction.

Cloning resolveChildStore instead of a generic owner/child resolver adds near-term duplication in exchange for lower risk and clearer store identity; deferred generalization is a reasonable YAGNI call.
Explicit separate fields (vs overloaded target_path) increase caller verbosity but eliminate ambiguity between owner-local-child-remote and owner-remote shapes.

documents.proposal:
# Fix remote Epic routing

## Why

ADV running in one project cannot treat another ADV project named by `target_path` as the authoritative target for Epic ownership and related change membership mutations. Operators coordinating from a business repo need to create or mutate Epics and changes in a product repo, including link/re-link/move/unlink/repair membership, without switching the OpenCode session into the product repo.

Current behavior observed from `/home/jon/dev/pokeedge-business` targeting `/home/jon/dev/pokeedge`:

- `adv_change_create target_path` with complete Epic seed fields created `planPricingTrust` in the target project but did not seed Epic membership.
- `adv_epic_link_change target_path` and `adv_epic_repair_membership target_path` reported `EPIC_NOT_FOUND` for `databaseOptimization`, even though related target-project child evidence referenced that Epic.

## What Changes

- Establish remote owner routing as a supported Epic/change operation shape.
- Ensure cross-project create/link/re-link/move/unlink/repair flows either operate against the target project as authoritative store or fail before mutation with a clear unsupported-routing error.
- Preserve audited trust confirmation and target project cache/projection correctness for remote mutations.
- Clarify documentation and ADV guidance for supported cross-project Epic ownership shapes.

## User Outcomes

- An operator running ADV in Project B can create an Epic in Project A when Project A is provided as the target project.
- An operator running ADV in Project B can create a Change in Project A when Project A is provided as the target project.
- An operator running ADV in Project B can link, re-link, move, unlink, or repair Project A Epic membership for Project A changes where the operation is supported.
- Unsupported cross-project owner/child splits fail early with actionable routing guidance instead of creating orphaned changes or returning misleading local-owner errors.
- Existing same-project and supported cross-project Epic flows remain valid.

## Scope

### In Scope

- Explicit separate owner/child routing fields for Epic operations that need to address Project A from Project B.
- Support for owner and child change living in different target projects in one call where the operation semantically needs both sides.
- Remote Epic owner routing for create/show/list/update/link/move/unlink/repair surfaces needed to operate from a coordinator repo.
- Create-time Epic membership seeding for `adv_change_create target_path` with complete Epic seed fields, with pre-create parent Epic validation.
- Clear pre-mutation rejection for unsupported or unserviceable routing shapes.
- Regression coverage for target-path Epic/change create and membership mutation behavior.
- Documentation updates that describe supported remote owner routing shapes and operator guidance.

### Out of Scope

- Introducing Jira-like planning primitives, assignments, sprints, estimates, or boards.
- Making Epic membership mandatory for all changes.
- Adding a new project-level shared workflow or replacing the per-change gate/task lifecycle.
- Arbitrary many-project graph orchestration beyond explicit owner/child routing for Epic membership.

# Design

## Architecture Overview

Implement explicit remote Epic-owner routing beside existing child-change routing.

Current Epic tools have one cross-project field family, `target_path` / `target_confirmed` / `confirmationEvidence`, and existing tests define that field as **child change routing**: the Epic parent remains current-session-local while the child projection may live in another ADV project. Issue #195 needs a different shape: ADV runs in Project B, but the Epic owner may live in Project A, and the child may also live in Project A or another Project C.

The design keeps current child routing semantics for backward compatibility and adds a second explicit owner routing field family for the Epic store:

- `epic_owner_target_path`
- `epic_owner_target_confirmed`
- `epic_owner_confirmationEvidence`

Existing child routing remains:

- `target_path`
- `target_confirmed`
- `confirmationEvidence`

A shared owner-store resolver maps the owner routing family into `withTargetPathStore` so owner reads/mutations use the routed Epic owner's Temporal-backed store/cache. Link/move/unlink/repair use two scoped stores when needed: owner store for `store.epics.*`, child store for `store.changes.*` projection updates.

## Key Decisions

### KD1 — Add explicit owner routing, do not overload `target_path`

`target_path` remains child-change routing for existing Epic membership tools. Remote Epic ownership uses `epic_owner_target_path`.

Rationale:

- User selected separate fields during discovery.
- `plugin/src/tools/epic.test.ts:625` currently encodes owner-local Epic + target child projection behavior.
- Overloading `target_path` would make two valid shapes indistinguishable and would break existing operators/tests.

### KD2 — Route every Epic-owner access through one owner accessor

Add an owner resolver analogous to `resolveChildStore`, for example:

```ts
async function resolveEpicOwnerStore(store, args) {
  if (!args.epic_owner_target_path) return { context: null, store };
  return withTargetPathStore({
    currentProjectPath: store.paths.root,
    target_path: args.epic_owner_target_path,
    stateRequirement: "temporal-required",
    target_confirmed: args.epic_owner_target_confirmed,
    confirmationEvidence: args.epic_owner_confirmationEvidence,
  }, async ({ context, store: ownerStore }) => ({ context, store: ownerStore }));
}
```

Use `ownerStore.store.epics.*` for every Epic lookup/mutation when owner routing is supplied. Avoid per-call one-off patches; the wrong-store bug is systemic across `loadEpic(store, ...)` and `store.epics.*` call sites.

### KD3 — Keep child projection routing independent

For link/move/unlink/repair, resolve child store from existing `target_path` unless the child can be proven same-owner and no child target is supplied.

Supported shapes:

| Shape | Owner route | Child route | Expected behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| Same project | omitted | omitted | Existing behavior unchanged |
| Owner local, child remote | omitted | `target_path` | Existing cross-project behavior unchanged |
| Owner remote, child same remote | `epic_owner_target_path=A` | `target_path=A` or omitted only when implementation can structurally prove same-owner child | Project B mutates Project A Epic and Project A child |
| Owner remote, child different remote | `epic_owner_target_path=A` | `target_path=C` | Project B mutates Project A Epic and Project C child projection |
| Unsupported / ambiguous | partial route, missing trust, no child locator when needed | any | Fail before durable mutation with typed routing error |

Design must not infer remote owner intent from `target_path` alone. Planning must include a deterministic same-owner-child proof or require an explicit child route.

### KD4 — Hoist Epic seed validation before `target_path` create short-circuit

`adv_change_create` currently branches to `createCrossProjectFollowUp` as soon as `target_path` exists. Therefore Epic seed validation must be hoisted before that branch, or AC1/SC3 cannot be enforced on the cross-project path.

Cross-project create behavior:

- If `target_path` is present and any Epic seed field is present, require complete seed fields.
- Require owner routing when parent Epic is not current project.
- Resolve owner store and validate parent Epic exists before calling `targetStore.changes.create`.
- If owner Epic cannot be read, target queue is unserviceable, trust confirmation is missing, or routing shape is unsupported, return a typed error and do not call child create.
- Forward `initialMetadata.epic_membership` into `createCrossProjectFollowUp` / target child create when validation succeeds.

Storage already accepts `initialMetadata.epic_membership`; the create-side fix is primarily validation ordering and metadata forwarding, not new persistence plumbing.

### KD5 — Return distinct routing contexts

When both owner and child routing are involved, output must not collapse both into one `_projectContext`. Use distinct contexts such as:

- `_epicOwnerProjectContext`
- `_childProjectContext`

For legacy single child-target operations, existing `_projectContext` may remain for compatibility, but new split-routing outputs should include explicit context names.

### KD6 — Add spec deltas and schema/tool-surface tests

This change alters public tool contracts. Add or update `advance-epics` requirements and generated docs/schema tests before implementation is considered complete.

## ADR Drafts

No ADR required. The routing field split is governed by ADV tool schema/spec contracts and does not need a separate ADR.

## Implementation Strategy

1. **Schema and helpers**
   - Define a reusable owner routing field group near `targetPathSchema` usage.
   - Add owner route args to relevant Epic tools and `adv_change_create`.
   - Implement `resolveEpicOwnerStore`, `appendEpicOwnerProjectContextOutput`, and explicit split-context output helpers.

2. **Remote Epic owner CRUD/read surfaces**
   - Add owner routing to `adv_epic_create`, `adv_epic_show`, `adv_epic_list`, `adv_epic_update`, `adv_epic_reorder`, `adv_epic_add_shell`, and safe same-owner shell promotion.
   - For owner-only tools, use owner store only.
   - If `adv_epic_promote_shell` without `change_id` would need remote child creation and cannot satisfy atomicity/trust safely, fail with `UNSUPPORTED_EPIC_ROUTING_SHAPE` until fully supported.

3. **Membership tools**
   - Add owner routing to `adv_epic_link_change`, `adv_epic_move_change`, `adv_epic_unlink_change`, and `adv_epic_repair_membership`.
   - Replace every `loadEpic(store, ...)` / `store.epics.*` in those tools with owner-store equivalents.
   - Keep `resolveChildStore` for child `store.changes.*` projection mutation.
   - Preflight owner and child target trust/readiness before first durable mutation when both sides are remote.
   - Preserve terminal child projection by passing owner store to `projectTerminalStateForLinkedEntry` and child change data from child store.

4. **Cross-project change create Epic seed**
   - Extend `createCrossProjectFollowUp` inputs to include complete Epic seed fields and owner route fields.
   - Hoist seed completeness and parent Epic validation before the `target_path` branch in `adv_change_create`.
   - Return stable typed errors before child create: `INVALID_EPIC_MEMBERSHIP_SEED`, `EPIC_OWNER_TARGET_REQUIRED`, `EPIC_NOT_FOUND`, `EPIC_OWNER_UNSERVICEABLE`, or `UNSUPPORTED_EPIC_ROUTING_SHAPE`.
   - Pass `initialMetadata: { cross_project_origin, epic_membership }` when seed validation succeeds.

5. **Tests**
   - RED: `adv_change_create target_path + Epic seed fields` validates parent and seeds membership; missing parent creates no child.
   - RED: source session + `epic_owner_target_path=A` + `target_path=A` uses target owner store for `epics.linkChange` and target child store for `changes.setEpicMembership`.
   - RED: split owner A / child C link or move enforces both target contexts and writes `change_ref.project_id`/`target_path` for child C.
   - RED: missing owner Epic returns typed error and neither parent nor child mutation is called.
   - RED: remote-child unsupported shell promotion fails before mutation with `UNSUPPORTED_EPIC_ROUTING_SHAPE`.
   - RED: owner mutation succeeds but child projection failure yields deterministic repair status or error path without silent success.
   - Regression: existing owner-local + child-remote test still passes.
   - Regression: same-project link/move/unlink/repair still passes.

6. **Docs/specs/schemas**
   - Add `advance-epics` requirements for remote owner routing, split owner/child membership, and create-time remote seed validation.
   - Update docs/spec mirrors, `ADV_INSTRUCTIONS.md`, command docs, tool descriptions, schema registry, generated JSON schemas, and asset tests.

## LBP Analysis

Preferred: explicit routing fields plus a supported routing matrix. This makes correctness structural:

- owner store and child store are separate typed concepts;
- trust confirmation is tied to the target being mutated;
- wrong-store `EPIC_NOT_FOUND` becomes avoidable;
- existing child-target semantics stay backward-compatible;
- split-project routing can be tested deterministically.

Rejected alternatives:

- **Single `target_path` means everything** — simpler call shape, but breaks/obscures existing owner-local child-target behavior.
- **Only fix create seed forwarding** — solves one symptom but leaves remote Epic create/link/repair impossible.
- **Generic resolver abstraction now** — possible later, but cloning proven `resolveChildStore` pattern is clearer and lower risk for this change.
- **Disk patching or direct state edits** — violates ADV state access and Temporal store invariants.

## Affected Components

- `plugin/src/tools/epic.ts`
- `plugin/src/tools/change.ts`
- `plugin/src/tools/change/create-clarify.ts`
- `plugin/src/tools/target-project.ts` or adjacent target-routing helper module
- `plugin/src/tool-registry.surface.test.ts`
- `plugin/src/tools/epic.test.ts`
- `plugin/src/tools/change.test.ts`
- `plugin/src/advance-epics-assets.test.ts`
- `plugin/src/schema-registry.ts` and generated `plugin/schemas/*.schema.json` if public schemas change
- `.adv/specs/advance-epics/spec.json` plus `docs/specs/advance-epics.md`
- `ADV_INSTRUCTIONS.md` and relevant `.opencode/command/adv-*.md` guidance

## Design-Derived Criteria

- DDC1: Owner and child target routing must be represented by distinct tool arguments and distinct output contexts when both are present.
- DDC2: Two-target membership tools must preflight all required target trust/readiness before first durable mutation.
- DDC3: New routing errors must include a stable `code` and name whether owner route, child route, or unsupported owner/child shape caused the failure.
- DDC4: Tests must assert store identity, not only success booleans, for owner and child mutations.
- DDC5: Epic seed validation must run before `adv_change_create` enters the target-path creation branch.
- DDC6: Same-owner-child omission must be structurally proven; otherwise require explicit child route.

## Risks / Mitigations

- Risk: Two remote stores are not transactionally atomic. Mitigation: preflight before mutation, preserve deterministic repair statuses, and keep projection repair tools available.
- Risk: Public tool schema grows. Mitigation: explicit field names, generated schema tests, and docs examples.
- Risk: Backward compatibility with child-only `target_path`. Mitigation: keep existing tests and semantics unless owner routing fields are supplied.
- Risk: Partial loadEpic patching leaves wrong-store failures. Mitigation: route all owner access through one owner accessor and assert store identity in tests.

## Design Leverage Scout

Scout result: pass/high confidence. Auto-adopted refinements:

- Hoist Epic seed validation before the `target_path` branch in `adv_change_create`; otherwise no-orphan AC is unreachable.
- Reuse existing `initialMetadata.epic_membership` persistence support instead of adding new storage plumbing.
- Treat wrong-store `loadEpic(store, ...)` as systemic and route all owner accesses through one owner accessor.
- Clone the proven `resolveChildStore` shape for owner routing rather than building a generic resolver in this change.

Deferred scout candidate:

- Generic owner/child resolver abstraction; defer until duplication proves problematic.

## Validator Result

Validator: pass, high confidence, low risk.

Source-verified findings:

- Wrong-store owner bug is systemic in Epic tools: membership tools call `store.epics.*` on current-session-local store while child projection alone uses `resolveChildStore`.
- Cross-project create seed drop is real: `adv_change_create` short-circuits on `target_path` before Epic seed assembly, and `createCrossProjectFollowUp` currently passes only `cross_project_origin`.
